winnerSummary: ED telehealth ads running 50+ days cluster around five proven patterns: (1) **Shame removal as the primary job** — the highest-longevity ads don't lead with efficacy, they lead with 'this is medical, not personal' or 'handle it privately.' The shame barrier is the real conversion blocker. (2) **Friction elimination in the hook** — 'no appointment, no waiting room, no awkward conversation' / '5-minute form' / 'delivered discreetly' address every step of the embarrassment chain. (3) **Price anchoring against brand-name drugs** — '$3 vs $70 same medication' is a uniquely high-performing angle because the audience already knows they want sildenafil/tadalafil; cost is the barrier. (4) **Medical authority** (urologist, real prescription, cardiologist) consistently outperforms lifestyle/aspirational framing — this audience is skeptical and educated about being sold to. (5) **Underused gap**: relationship cost angle (wife thought I lost interest) runs far fewer ads than product/price angles despite its emotional power. Brands running relationship-narrative ads tend to have longer run durations.
